Ingredients:
Flour – 2 cups,Water – 2 cups (or as needed)
,Salt – 1 tsp,Butter – 1 tbsp (optional, for serving)
Instruction:
Pour the required amount of water into a pan.
Add salt and bring the water to a boil.
Gradually add the flour while stirring continuously.
Mix well until the flour absorbs all the water and forms a smooth, thick dough without lumps.
Cook for 3–5 minutes on low heat while stirring.
Transfer the prepared mixture to a serving plate.
Shape or decorate it using a spoon or spatula.
Serve hot with butter, ghee, or your preferred side dish.

Ingredients:
Wheat Flour – 2 cups,Water – 1½ cups (or as needed),Salt – 1 tsp
Yeast – 1 tsp,Onion Leaves (Spring Onion) – ½ cup (chopped),
Fresh Coriander (Dhaniya) – ½ cup (chopped),
Sour Yogurt or Sour Gravy (optional, for a tangy taste) – ½ cup,
Plain Yogurt or Regular Gravy (optional, for a mild taste) – ½ cup
Instruction:
Take the wheat flour in a large bowl.
Add salt, yeast, and enough water to make a soft dough.
Mix well and knead until the dough becomes smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rest for about 20 minutes.
After resting, divide the dough into small pieces and shape them as desired.
Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Carefully place the shaped dough pieces into the boiling water and cook until they are fully done and float to the surface.
In a separate bowl, prepare the sauce by mixing chopped onion leaves and fresh coriander.
Add either sour yogurt/gravy for a tangy flavor or plain yogurt/gravy for a mild flavor, then mix well.
Remove the cooked dough pieces from the boiling water and drain them.
Pour the prepared sauce over the cooked pieces and mix gently.
Serve hot and enjoy.

Ingredients:
Wheat Flour – 2 cups
Milk – 1 cup
Yogurt – 2 tbsp
Ghee – 2 tbsp,Salt – 1 tsp,Sugar – 1 tsp (optional, for a slightly sweet taste),
Yeast – 1 tsp
Instruction:
Take the wheat flour in a large mixing bowl.
Add milk, yogurt, ghee, salt, sugar (optional), and yeast.
Mix all the ingredients well and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover the dough with a clean cloth and let it rest for about 1 hour so it rises properly.
Lightly grease a flat pan (tawa) with ghee.
Take a portion of the dough and shape it by hand into a round flatbread, keeping it about 1 inch thick.
Place it on the heated tawa and cook on low heat for 8–10 minutes on one side until it turns golden brown.
Flip it carefully and cook the other side for another 8 minutes, or until both sides are evenly browned and fully cooked.
Remove from the tawa and brush with a little extra ghee if desired.
Serve hot with a cup of warm tea. ?

Ingredients:
Tro – 500 g,Tranma – 300 g,Onion – 2 medium (sliced),
Garlic – 6 cloves (chopped),Onion Leaves (Spring Onion) – ½ cup (chopped),
Fresh Coriander (Dhaniya) – ½ cup (chopped),
Salt – 1 tsp (or to taste),
Turmeric Powder – ½ tsp,
Mixed Vegetable Masala – 1 tsp,
Oil – 3 tbsp,
Water – 2–3 cups (or as needed)
Instruction:
Heat the oil in a pressure cooker over medium heat.
Add the sliced onions and sauté until they turn golden brown.
Add the chopped garlic and cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the mixed vegetable masala, salt, and turmeric powder, then stir well.
Mix in the chopped onion leaves and fresh coriander.
Add the Tro and Tranma, then stir well so they are evenly coated with the spices.
Pour in enough water according to the desired consistency.
Close the pressure cooker and cook for 10–15 minutes after the pressure builds.
Turn off the heat and allow the pressure to release naturally.
Open the cooker, stir gently, and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Serve hot with Balti bread, chapati, or rice.
